![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131939/assets/cbe865077b446bdd97c290cef0924d3f17807a9e1039c9be45f4aa6e4b29cc3c.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=1,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=5,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-3,
$$

where ${C}_{1},$ ${C}_{2},$ and ${C}_{3}$ are oriented counterclockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131939/assets/fd221ae68fc4983fb0a3f7a745154764e5c0081b2b9b66e7f8ad4a150a8b3bc5.png)

Notice that the positive orientations of the inner curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ are opposite to those stated in the question.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =1-5-(-3) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
